segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly I tell you, there are some standing here who will certainly not taste death until they see that the kingdom of God has come in power.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Six days later Jesus took Peter, James, and John and led them up a high mountain, privately, by themselves. And he was transformed before them,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and his clothes became dazzling, intensely white, whiter than any launderer on earth could whiten them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Elijah appeared to them with Moses, and they were talking with Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter spoke up and said to Jesus,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Rabbi, it is good that we are here. Let us make three tents: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For he did not know what to say, because they were terrified.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then a cloud came and overshadowed them, and a voice came from the cloud:

segments.speaker: God
segments.text: “This is my Son, the beloved; listen to him!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Suddenly, when they looked around, they no longer saw anyone, but only Jesus with them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As they were coming down from the mountain, he ordered them to tell no one what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They kept the matter to themselves, debating what this rising from the dead meant.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they asked him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Elijah does come first and restores all things. Yet how is it written about the Son of Man that he must suffer much and be treated with contempt?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But I tell you that Elijah has in fact come, and they did to him whatever they wanted, just as it is written about him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they came to the disciples, they saw a large crowd around them and scribes debating with them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Immediately the whole crowd, when they saw him, were struck with amazement, and they ran up and greeted him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He asked them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “What are you debating with them?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One of the crowd answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, I brought my son to you; he has a mute spirit.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Wherever it seizes him, it throws him down, and he foams at the mouth and grinds his teeth and goes rigid. I asked your disciples to drive it out, but they were not strong enough.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You unbelieving generation! How long am I to be with you? How long am I to put up with you? Bring him to me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They brought the boy to him. When the spirit saw him, it immediately convulsed the boy, and he fell to the ground and rolled about, foaming at the mouth.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus asked the boy’s father,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “How long has this been happening to him?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Since childhood.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: It has often thrown him even into fire and into water to destroy him. But if you can do anything, have compassion on us and help us.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “‘If you can’! All things are possible for the one who believes.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Immediately the child’s father cried out,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I believe; help my unbelief!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Jesus saw that a crowd was running together, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You mute and deaf spirit, I command you: come out of him and never enter him again.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After crying out and convulsing him violently, it came out. The boy became like a corpse, so that most of them were saying he had died.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus took him by the hand and raised him up, and he rose to his feet.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he had gone into a house, his disciples asked him privately,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Why could we not drive it out?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “This kind can come out by nothing except prayer.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They left that place and were passing through Galilee, and he did not want anyone to know,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for he was teaching his disciples and saying to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “The Son of Man is being handed over into human hands, and they will kill him, and when he has been killed, after three days he will rise.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But they did not understand the saying, and they were afraid to ask him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They came to Capernaum. When he was in the house, he asked them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “What were you discussing on the way?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But they were silent, for on the way they had argued with one another about who was the greatest.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He sat down, called the Twelve, and said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Anyone who wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he took a little child and stood the child in their midst, and taking the child in his arms, he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Whoever welcomes one child like this in my name welcomes me; and whoever welcomes me welcomes not me but the one who sent me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: John said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, we saw someone driving out demons in your name, and we tried to stop him, because he was not following us.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Do not stop him, for no one who does a deed of power in my name will be able soon afterward to speak evil of me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For whoever is not against us is for us.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink because you belong to Christ, truly I tell you, will certainly not lose their reward.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for that person if a large millstone were hung around their neck and they were thrown into the sea.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life maimed than, having two hands, to go away into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than, having two feet, to be thrown into Gehenna.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And if your eye causes you to stumble, throw it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God one-eyed than, having two eyes, to be thrown into Gehenna,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: where ‘their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For everyone will be salted with fire.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Salt is good; but if the salt loses its saltiness, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”

notes.note: The traditional 'transfigured' comes from the Latin translation and is now used almost only of this event. The Greek verb is the ordinary word for a change of form or appearance, and Paul uses it for the change in believers (Romans 12:2; 2 Corinthians 3:18). 'Transformed' gives what a first-century reader heard, though most translations keep 'transfigured'.

notes.traditional: they kept that saying with themselves
notes.note: The Greek can be divided two ways. Either they kept the matter to themselves, obeying the order to tell no one, or they seized on the saying and debated it among themselves. Both readings are found in modern translations.

Malachi 4:5–6 promises that Elijah will be sent before the day of the Lord to restore the people, and scribal teaching drew on this. Jesus accepts the expectation and says it has already been fulfilled. Matthew's parallel (17:13) says the disciples understood him to mean John the Baptist, whose arrest and execution Mark has already told.

The verb normally means to dry up or wither. Here it may describe the boy's body stiffening during a seizure, which is how most recent translations take it. It may instead describe him becoming exhausted or wasting away over time, as older versions have it.

In the earliest manuscripts Jesus throws the father's own words back at him. Many later manuscripts add 'believe', which produces the traditional 'If you can believe, all things are possible'. Editors generally regard the shorter reading as original and the addition as a scribe's attempt to smooth an abrupt phrase.

Most later manuscripts add 'and fasting'. The words are absent from a few of the earliest and most important manuscripts and are omitted here, following the Greek text being translated. Most scholars see them as an early addition reflecting church practice, though some defend the longer reading.

The verb means to hand someone over into another's control. 'Betrayed' narrows it to Judas's act, but the text does not say who does the handing over; it may be Judas, or God, as in Isaiah 53 in the Greek Old Testament. The Greek also plays on 'Son of Man' being given into the hands of 'men', here rendered 'human hands'.

The verb pictures tripping someone up or setting a trap in their path, and in the Gospels it is used of whatever causes a person to fall away from faith or into sin. Older versions have 'offend', which now suggests merely hurting feelings, and several modern ones have 'cause to sin'. 'Cause to stumble' keeps the image and the breadth of the Greek, and is also used by a number of modern translations.
The Greek is literally 'a donkey millstone', the heavy upper stone of a mill turned by a donkey, as distinct from the small hand mill used in a household.

Gehenna is a place name, the Valley of Hinnom outside Jerusalem, which had become the standard Jewish image for the place of final judgment. 'Hell' merges it with Hades and with much later imagery, so the name is kept here. Many translations still use 'hell', usually with a footnote giving Gehenna.

Verses 44 and 46 do not appear in this translation. In later manuscripts each of them repeats the words of verse 48, but they are absent from the earliest manuscripts and from the Greek text translated here. Most modern translations omit them while keeping the traditional verse numbers.

notes.phrase: their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched
notes.note: The words come from the last verse of Isaiah (66:24). There they describe the corpses of those who rebelled against God lying outside Jerusalem.

notes.traditional: For every one shall be salted with fire, and every sacrifice shall be salted with salt
notes.note: Later manuscripts add 'and every sacrifice will be salted with salt', echoing Leviticus 2:13; the earliest manuscripts have only the short form translated here. The meaning of the saying is disputed. It may refer to purifying trials that every disciple undergoes, or to the fire of judgment just mentioned.

candidates.reason: Recurs across the Gospels and Paul, and translations vary between 'offend', 'cause to sin', 'cause to stumble' and 'fall away', which obscures a single image.
Used throughout the passion predictions and narratives; alternating between 'betray', 'deliver' and 'hand over' hides the repeated verb and prejudges who the agent is.
Frequent in the Gospels; 'scribe' suggests a copyist to modern readers, while 'scholar' or 'teacher of the law' are plausible alternatives, so one decision is needed.
In its sense of a miraculous act it is rendered variously 'miracle', 'mighty work' and 'deed of power', and it should stay linked to 'power' elsewhere, as in 9:1.
Jesus's characteristic self-designation across all four Gospels; its capitalisation and wording ('Son of Man' or 'Human One' or 'son of man') need one ruling.
